title: Tomo Instructions
description: Canonical, machine-readable instruction set produced by instruction-render.py. Consumed by Tomo Hashi (Obsidian plugin) for execution and rendered to a human-readable markdown view.

source_suggestions.description: Filename (vault-relative or stem) of the suggestions doc this set was derived from.

tomo_version.description: Tomo version that produced this file.

md_peer.description: Stem of the companion human-readable markdown, in the same folder (e.g. '2026-04-21_0918_instructions'). Explicit linkage rather than inferred from timestamp/convention — lets Tomo Hashi refuse with a clear error when the peer is missing or renamed. Always populated by instruction-render.py v0.6.0+; not in the required set so v0.5.x artefacts still validate.

tomo.description: Tomo lifecycle/provenance metadata mirroring the human-readable .md frontmatter (doc_type/state/run_id/sources). Tomo-owned; Hashi ignores it for execution — Hashi only runs `actions`. Optional and additive: instruction sets without this block still validate. Kept permissive (no additionalProperties:false) so Tomo can evolve the block without a coordinated round-trip (tomo-to-hashi handoff 2026-06-20, miyo-tomo#74).

skipped_daily.description: Daily-note update actions the renderer dropped because their target daily note does not exist (Hashi cannot create daily notes). Metadata only — no note content. Consumed by instructions-diff to reconcile expected vs actual coverage; Hashi ignores it.

action_id.description: Monotonic action identifier (I01, I02, …). Unique within the instruction set.

applied_field.description: True when Tomo Hashi has successfully executed this action. Defaults to false on emission. Monotonic — Hashi only writes false → true; Tomo never re-emits true. Optional for v0.5.x backwards-compat (missing = treated as false).

source.description: Vault-relative full path of the rendered file currently in the inbox (what gets moved), e.g. '100 Inbox/2026-04-21_1200_asahikawa-....md'.

destination.description: Vault-relative full target path including the final filename, e.g. 'Atlas/202 Notes/Asahikawa — ....md'.

title.description: Final title of the note (also the stem of the destination filename).

rendered_file.description: Basename of the rendered file (redundant with source; kept for display).

source_inbox_item.description: Optional vault-relative path of the original inbox item this note was derived from. The delete_source action is the operational signal for cleanup; by default the renderer emits a paired delete_source for this source unless the user opts out via the suggestions doc's 'Keep source files' checkbox.

target_moc_path.description: Resolved vault-relative path of the MOC, if known.

anchor.description: Where in the target MOC to find the insertion point. type=callout matches the callout opening line; type=heading matches a heading by text; type=line matches a body line by content.

placement.description: Where to write relative to the matched anchor. inside (callout only) appends as last line of callout body with > prefix. after inserts immediately after the matched anchor's terminal line, verbatim. before inserts immediately before the matched anchor's first line, verbatim.

line_to_add.description: Pre-formatted content to insert (bullet style, link form, etc. all decided Tomo-side). May be multi-line (embedded \n) to insert a block such as a new section heading plus its first bullet. Hashi writes the content verbatim for placement=after/before; for placement=inside on a callout anchor it prepends '> ' to each line.

type.description: callout = match callout opening line (e.g. '[!blocks] Key Concepts'); heading = match heading text without # prefix (any heading level); line = match body line by literal content; block = match N consecutive lines, the value's \n-joined lines, each exact after trimming trailing whitespace — for unique multi-row markers (e.g. a table's header row + separator row together) that a single line anchor cannot express. inside is unsupported for block.

value.description: Content of the anchor to match. Null is permitted only at emission time when the renderer cannot resolve a concrete value yet (resolver populates later via Kado read).

target_moc.description: MOC stem for human-readable display (no path, no .md).

target_moc_path.description: Resolved vault-relative path of the target MOC.

marker.description: Dataview inline-field marker that locates the line to replace, e.g. 'up::' or 'related::'. Hashi locates the first line whose stripped content (after optional '> ' callout prefix) starts with this marker.

line.description: Pre-formatted full line content to write, e.g. 'up:: [[Hobbies (MOC)]]' or 'related:: [[A]], [[B]]'. Hashi replaces the located marker line with this verbatim, preserving the line's leading '> ' prefix if the marker was inside a callout. Multi-link aggregation for related:: is done Tomo-side.

section.description: Daily log heading (e.g. 'Daily Log'), without leading #.

source.description: Vault-relative full path of the rendered MOC file currently in the inbox, e.g. '100 Inbox/2026-04-21_1200_brettspiele-moc.md'.

destination.description: Vault-relative full target path of the MOC, e.g. 'Atlas/200 Maps/Brettspiele (MOC).md'.

rendered_file.description: Basename of the rendered MOC file (redundant with source; kept for display).

parent_moc.description: Parent MOC stem for up-linking (emitted separately as an add_relationship action with marker='up::' on this MOC).

supporting_items.description: Supporting items that justify the new MOC. String (comma-separated SNN IDs from suggestion-parser, e.g. 'S02, S06, S12') or array (note stems from moc-proposal-parser, e.g. ['Thought Collisions', 'Map of Content']). Human context — link_to_moc actions are the executable signal.

insert_under_marker.description: Insert a multi-line markdown block under a heading/anchor marker in an arbitrary vault note. Reuses the shared `anchor` $def; `placement` uses the same inline enum as `link_to_moc`. Modify-only — Tomo guarantees the target_path and anchor exist before emitting. Introduced by spec 024-tag-handler-framework (T1.1a handoff 2026-06-23).

target_path.description: Vault-relative path to the target note (full path, not a MOC stem). Tomo guarantees the note exists before emitting this action.

anchor.description: Where in the target note to find the insertion point. type=heading matches heading text without '#' prefix (most common for this action); type=callout and type=line are also valid.

placement.description: Where to insert content relative to the matched anchor. inside (heading) = beneath the matched heading, above the next same-or-higher-level heading. before/after keep standard semantics.

content.description: Multi-line markdown block to insert verbatim. May contain embedded newlines. Hashi inserts as-is without transformation.

edit_note_text.description: Edit note body by exact literal string match and replacement. One primitive covers dead-wikilink fix (replace='[[New]]'), dead-wikilink remove (replace=''), and broken up:: removal (whole-line match, replace=''). Hashi skips and reports on no-match — no error, no partial write. Broken-up REPOINT uses add_relationship (marker-located line replace), not this action. Introduced by spec 030-garden-audit ADR-3 (example-driven: Tomo emits this now; Hashi implements against our real example in Phase 6 handoff).

path.description: Vault-relative path of the note to edit (.md).

match.description: Exact literal text to locate in the note body, e.g. '[[Missing Note]]' or 'up:: [[Old MOC]]'.

replace.description: Replacement text. Empty string removes the matched text (and the now-empty line when match covers a whole line).

occurrence.description: Which occurrence(s) to replace. 'first' (default) replaces only the first match; 'all' replaces every occurrence.

remove_up_link.description: Remove ONE link from the note's up:: line (broken_up empty=remove, link-only semantics — user decision 2026-07-23). Hashi locates the up:: line with the same marker regex as add_relationship and removes the [[link]] occurrence on that line INCLUDING a dangling separator (e.g. 'up:: [[A]], [[X]]' → 'up:: [[A]]'). CRITICAL: the up:: FIELD is preserved — when the removed link was the only one, the line becomes an empty 'up::' ('up:: [[X]]' → 'up:: '), it is NOT deleted. up:: is a required structural field; an emptied up:: correctly resurfaces the note as unparented next scan. Skip-and-report on no-match (no up:: line, or link not on it) — no error, no partial write. Replaces the earlier whole-line edit_note_text construction, which silently no-opped on multi-link up:: lines.

path.description: Vault-relative path of the note whose up:: line is edited (.md).

link.description: Bare stem of the link to remove from the up:: line, e.g. 'Deleted MOC' (no [[ ]]).
